title: The pyramid builders were not slaves.
description:
The pyramid builders were not slaves. Harvard Magazine reported Mark Lehner's discovery of the city of the pyramid builders, and put it plainly.

Herodotus gets the credit for the slave story. AP says he described the builders as slaves. A translation quoted by Ancient Origins says that passage uses no word for slaves.

First found in the backyard of the Giza pyramids, according to AP. Hawass said the dead were buried near their pharaohs' pyramids.

The crews named themselves. Harvard says early graffiti named gangs such as Friends of Khufu and Drunkards of Menkaure.

Plus 23 sheep, sent in every day for about 10,000 labourers, according to AP in 2010. The team also found the oldest bakery ever found in Egypt.

It was still brutal work. AP reports skeletons with arthritis and strained lower backs. Hawass said most fractures had healed well, indicating splints.

Fed, housed and buried beside the king's pyramid.

Sources:
- https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2003/07/who-built-the-pyramids.html: read (Harvard Magazine, Jonathan Shaw, 1 July 2003). Established that Mark Lehner found the city of the pyramid builders and that "They were not slaves"; two towns side by side; the oldest bakery found in Egypt; young, mostly male cattle, enough to feed several thousand people even if they ate meat every day; and that Reisner found workers' graffiti naming gangs such as Friends of Khufu or Drunkards of Menkaure.
- https://phys.org/news/2010-01-egypt-slaves-didnt-pyramids.pdf: read (AP report, 10 January 2010). Established that graves of the pyramid builders were first discovered in the area in 1990 in the backyard of the Giza pyramids; that about 10,000 labourers ate 21 cattle and 23 sheep sent daily from farms; that workers ate meat regularly and worked in three month shifts; that Herodotus, who visited around 450 BC, described the builders as slaves; and that skeletons show arthritis and a hard life.
- https://www.ancient-origins.net/news-history-archaeology/giza-pyramids-built-by-slaves-builders-evidence-00128327: read (fact check, secondary). Used only for the Loeb translation point that the Herodotus passage uses no word for slaves, and Hawass's statement that most fractures had healed well, indicating splints.
